Where is my save?

Choose the Big Ambitions folder inside SaveGames; the page finds the newest save across the company folders inside it.

If you cannot find it, the game shows you: on its Load Game screen, click Browse savegame folder… and the folder opens in a file window.

The game autosaves every five minutes. Your browser may call folder access an "upload" or ask to "let this site view files"; the save stays on your computer. Checked on game build 3682; the Python runtime the page needs is about 6 MB, fetched once and cached.

Linked to the game. With the Big Copilot Link mod from the Steam Workshop enabled, click Link to the game and the board reads the running game itself. Chrome and Edge ask once to allow the site to reach your computer; the data still never leaves it.

Game text

Names, recipes and station capacities come with the page, from game build 3682.

If your game is newer, click the chip and choose its en.json; it is remembered in this browser and wins over the built-in text.

en.json lives here · default Windows Steam installation
C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Big Ambitions\Big Ambitions_Data\StreamingAssets\locale

To find your game's en.json, open Steam → Manage → Browse local files. On macOS, search that folder for en.json; use Show Package Contents if the game files are inside an app bundle.

· the page only reads your saves, from a folder or from the running game.

· undo

Changelog

What's changed in Big Copilot.

  1. 25 Sep 2026PR #153 ↗

    Goods flow you can read on a phone

    On a phone or a portrait tablet, Supply's goods-flow diagram is now a chain you read top to bottom: your importers, depots, factories and shops in the order the goods travel, with the pipes between them. A depot's shops fold into one card from four up, the sites worth a look sit in a row on top, and shops no pipe reaches share one line at the bottom. Tap a site to follow it: what comes in, what goes out, the pipe carrying a short or stalled product in colour, its problems in words, and one tap to its rows or its site page. With no pipe yet, the box says so and links the wiki's guide to imports.

  2. 25 Sep 2026PR #121 ↗

    Hire and place staff for every site at once

    Company › Payroll is now Staff. It adds up what each shop, office and factory still needs by role, moves spare people between sites first, and picks the most skilled of your headhunters' candidates, with filters for the demands you want to avoid. One confirm hires them, puts them at their sites and writes their hours, through the Big Copilot Link mod 0.3.0. Hires cannot be undone.

  3. 25 Sep 2026PR #118 ↗

    Game names in the language you play in

    A new Game names setting in the footer, beside Theme, shows the game's own names in any language the game ships: items, business types, neighbourhoods, stations, skills and staff demands, on the board, inside its findings and in the wiki, so the board reads like your game. The rest of the page stays English. Search finds a name in either language, and lists sort in the language you picked. If your browser prefers one of the game's languages, the board asks once whether to use it.

  4. 25 Sep 2026PR #114 ↗

    Supply by shop, warehouse and factory, and staffing for factory lines

    Supply is now three tabs, one per object: Shops, Warehouses and Factories. Each opens on what needs a change, with the figure to type beside the setting it changes and a tick at the head of the row; one checklist under the tabs counts your ticks across all three and copies what is left. Idle stock folds into one row per warehouse or per cause, a shelf topped up far above what it sells gets a lower target to type, and the goods-flow diagram is a view of each tab: click a site to see its rows. Factories shows the hours each line is rostered against the hours it needs, 24/7 or for what your shops use, and too few hours is a change to type. A new Staffing for factory lines block gives each line's shifts, the factory workers the plan needs against those you have, and what the difference does to your wages. This answers the voted request "Supply chain for factories not running 24/7".

  5. 25 Sep 2026PR #113 ↗

    Floor plans for every building, and a Layout filter

    Each building the finder lists now names its layout, the game's short code for its shape, such as C1 or H3. Click a building on the map or in the list and its card shows the game's own floor plan for it, with its entrances (loading bays for a warehouse). A new Layout filter in Find a location lists only the layouts you pick, and a saved search keeps it.

  6. 24 Sep 2026PR #94 ↗

    Size supply for 24/7 or for demand, and find stock no plan sends on

    Supply now judges every item once and uses the same word for it everywhere: covered, tight, short, no plan, paused, stalled, idle, made here or new. A Sizing switch on Orders, on the factory and import checks and on each warehouse and factory page sizes your factory lines, top-ups and imports for 24/7 rated output or for what your shops actually use, with one 15% margin over the whole chain from import to sale and figures rounded up to tens. Under Demand, a shop open less than a week is projected forward and marked "may still be ramping". Tight means an order covers the use but not the margin; it shows on Supply and never on Today. Shops and warehouses stocked by a repeating wholesale contract are judged against it. A new Not routed finding points at stock in a warehouse or factory that no plan sends on while your own shops sell it.

  7. 24 Sep 2026PR #83 ↗

    Fix: warehouses fed by your own factory no longer read as short

    A warehouse your own factory tops up every morning on a logistics route was flagged as a critical import shortfall for every item the factory delivers, often with an alert that weekly orders cannot cover their week and a large one-off to bring in. The board now counts what your factories bring on routes before it judges the import, so a backup import next to such a route no longer raises the alarm, paused or not. If a route brings only part of what leaves, the import is sized on the rest, and a busy day that could still empty the shelf before the next morning's round is still flagged. The Factories page takes the same routes into account.

  8. 24 Sep 2026PR #82 ↗

    Write to the game from the board (Big Copilot Link 0.2.0)

    With the Big Copilot Link mod 0.2.0, the board can now make three changes in your game for you: set uniforms where roles have none, apply the import amounts from Plan imports, and write a shop's staffing plan, for one shop or a run of shops. Every change shows what the game will do before you apply it, can be undone once, and is refused, with nothing written, if the game has moved on since the board last read it. The first write from a browser asks for approval in the game; after that it is remembered.

  9. 24 Sep 2026PR #81 ↗

    Every site has its own page, and you can search the board

    Each shop, warehouse, factory and office now opens as its own page with an address, so a reload keeps it and Back and Forward walk between sites; a crumb takes you back to where you came from, and site names on Today, Supply and the map link to it. Press / or Ctrl+K to search the whole board: pages, your sites, products, kinds of finding, location presets and the game's help pages, with everyday words like hire, debt or difficulty. Today has an Ask the board row whose questions land on the answer. The difficulty you play on sits beside the clock, and Company › Results can show your week by weekday.

  10. 23 Sep 2026PR #77 ↗

    Full cover for a new shop, and a demand plan after 9 days

    A new shop can now run a demand test: the Staffing block offers Full cover 24/7 beside its usual plan, every serving station staffed every hour with the fewest people the game's rules allow, and a step to open every day 0 to 24. Nine days after the shop's first customer the board has the shop's own week and gives it the demand plan, without waiting two weeks. Hours nobody came count as no customers. When the data is in and the shop is still fully staffed, the Staffing block and Today say to switch to the demand plan. Plans now say in one step how many people to add: who to assign from your unassigned staff and how many to hire, and hire counts are the true minimum.

  11. 23 Sep 2026PR #76 ↗

    Imports that read Smart Delivery, and your own order figures

    The weekly imports now understand the purchasing agent's Smart Delivery setting: its amount is a stock level the agent tops up to each Monday, not a delivery, and the board judges it that way, in the order the game delivers your contracts. The imports table shows what arrived last week, what is set in game ("in stock" or "a week"), and a Set to box with the board's suggestion that you can change. Your figures carry into the Plan imports checklist, which names the importer to change when a material has more than one contract. For Smart Delivery the suggestion is the stock that runs everything the depot feeds at full capacity for a week, so it only moves when your capacity does.

  12. 23 Sep 2026PR #75 ↗

    No more gas station tips

    Big Copilot will no longer tell you to open a gas station. Or a wholesaler. Or a casino. The city runs those itself and is not selling, however good the numbers look. Market demand and Find a location now suggest only business types you can actually open, straight from the game's own F1 help, including ones nobody in your city runs yet.

  13. 22 Sep 2026PR #68 ↗

    Link to the game

    A third way in beside the save folder and the single file: with the Big Copilot Link mod from the Steam Workshop enabled, click Link to the game and the board reads the running game itself. No folder to pick, and the board follows the game as you play: it refreshes on the game hour, after a game save, and whenever you click Update. The mod serves the game's own save to this page on your computer and to nothing else; Chrome and Edge ask once to allow the site to reach it. The local watcher learnt the same trick as --game.

  14. 21 Sep 2026PR #64 ↗

    Contributions welcome

    Help improve Big Copilot with fixes, features, docs or tests. The GitHub README now has a short contribution guide: focused PRs, mockups to discuss bigger ideas, test results and agent review for AI-written code.

  15. 20 Sep 2026PR #61 ↗

    Staffing, in hours and days you can act on

    The staffing plan now builds a week one person can really work. Nobody is spread across two businesses, hours stay inside the full-time band the game pays for, and somebody who asked for four days a week gets four, not five. A shop the board cannot read yet says so and covers its cleaning and security in the meantime, instead of offering to clear a schedule that nothing here could put back. The block is now called Staffing and speaks the game's own language: hours and days rather than shifts, entries you copy into BizMan one day at a time, stations by name with the short codes on hover, and people to hire rather than posts, each sized at the 30 hours a week a full-time employee is owed. It also says what makes its numbers worth reading, which is two weeks with every station staffed. Building capacity replaces "door cap" on the board and in the location finder.

  16. 19 Sep 2026PR #58 ↗

    A page for every site, and a week of staffing to copy in

    Every site's page now leads with the warnings about that site, and hovering one lights the part of the page that shows why. Shops and offices gain a profit rank among your trading sites, trend sparks and a cost bar, satisfaction against the 80 line with a lamp for each amenity, what pulls customers in, the ceiling each busy hour ran into, and a crew view that folds big rosters into one row per role. Depots and factories get pages of their own for the first time: a seven-day rail for each item with its delivery truck, what each depot feeds, a square for every machine filled by how much of the week it is staffed, and the inputs each line eats. A home opens from its map card. Shops also get Staffing: a week of hours to copy into BizMan, cut so that nobody works more than the 12 hours a day the game allows, people placed where their schedule demands hold, cleaning and security covered, and how many to hire for each station. Tick each entry off as you set it. The Optimize staffing card on Today opens the shop where it saves the most work. Gyms, hairdressers, theatres and nightclubs now get at-the-ceiling and overstaffed warnings, and switching a warning kind off moves its smaller findings to the bottom of the list and says so.

  17. 19 Sep 2026PR #56 ↗

    A Discord to talk it over in

    The footer's Follow column now links a Discord server for Big Ambitions and Big Copilot: somewhere to ask what a number means, compare saves and strategies, and say what the board should show next. The invite is in the footer on the landing screen and on the board, beside YouTube and the subreddit.

  18. 18 Sep 2026PR #50 ↗

    Choose light or dark

    The footer now has a theme control: match your system, or pin the board to light or dark. The choice is remembered in your browser and is applied before the page draws, so returning to it never flashes the other palette. Scrollbars and drop-downs follow the theme you picked instead of staying with your operating system's.

  19. 17 Sep 2026PR #43 ↗

    Warnings for unmet staff demands

    Needs attention now tells you when your employees' demands are not met, at every kind of site: the schedule they asked for, equipment at their desk, a water cooler or fridge in the building, a clean workplace. Each site gets one line naming what is missing and for how many staff, and health insurance and a happy boss go on one company line. The line turns critical once someone with an unmet demand has warned they will quit, and a site's page lists the demands under its crew.

  20. 16 Sep 2026PR #40 ↗

    Staffing by the hour for offices

    Law firms, travel agencies and the other office businesses now get the same Customers by hour grid as shops, with staff at computers as their capacity, and the same warnings when they sit at the ceiling or have staff standing idle. Offices form their own chain in the Portfolio and list their fee instead of shelves. The at-the-ceiling warning for shops and offices now names the right limit for each hour.

  21. 16 Sep 2026PR #34 ↗

    Save your location searches

    The location finder can keep its filters and sort as a named search. Saved searches sit in a new Saved row, are shared by all your characters and apply in one click. The finder also stays open when you visit another page and come back.

  22. 16 Sep 2026PR #34 ↗

    Click a column header in Supply's stock checks, weekly imports or daily top-ups to sort by it, click again to reverse, or pick "usual order" to put the rows back. Imports and top-ups sort within each depot or factory.

Any building's card now shows its owner, renter, size, cap, traffic and rent. The Today card counts vacant units, a Growth cell jumps to premises for its type, and the Wiki explains how rent works.

  25. 14 Sep 2026PR #27 ↗

Law firms, travel agencies and the other office businesses appear in their own band, read from their hourly fee, with your own office outlined.

  26. 14 Sep 2026PR #26 ↗
